questions.prompt: The provider answers 401 because the API key is wrong. What should the retry logic do?
options: Retry 5 times with backoff, then give up
Retry once immediately, then give up
Fail at once, because a wrong key fails the same way every time
Retry until the provider sends a Retry-After header
questions.explanation: AUTH is not in the retryable set. Waiting cannot fix a wrong key, so retrying only wastes about 15 seconds before failing anyway.

questions.prompt: With an initial delay of 500 ms doubling each time and a 10,000 ms cap, about how long is the wait before the fourth retry?
questions.explanation: The waits are 500 times 2 to the power (retry minus 1): 500, 1000, 2000, then 4000 ms for the fourth retry, give or take 10% jitter.

questions.prompt: Why add jitter, a small random amount, to each wait?
options: So clients that failed together do not all retry at the same moment
So the model gets a different answer each time
So the total wait never exceeds the cap
So the provider can tell retries apart from new requests
questions.explanation: If many clients fail at once and wait exactly the same time, they all retry together and overload the provider again. A random spread separates them.
